question: Who among the following Indian music directors, specially known as a leading drummer of India, was awarded the Padma Shri in 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sivamani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sivamani (Anandan Sivamani) is one of India's most celebrated percussionists and drummers, renowned for his versatility across genres including Carnatic, jazz, rock and film music. (शिवमणि — ड्रमर, पद्म श्री 2019)

 

• He was conferred the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian award, in 2019 for his contribution to art (percussion/music).

 

• He rose to fame through collaborations with A.R. Rahman, Zakir Hussain, and as a member of the fusion band Shakti and the group Colonial Cousins.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sivamani is known for his signature use of kitchen utensils and everyday objects as percussion instruments during live performances.

 

• He has performed and recorded with numerous international artists and has been part of many Bollywood and Kollywood film scores.

 

NOTE

 

• Nucleya (Option 2): A prominent Indian electronic/EDM music producer, not a Padma Shri awardee in 2019.

 

• Bappi Lahiri (Option 3): A legendary music composer/singer known as the 'Disco King' of India; he passed away in 2022 and was not the 2019 Padma Shri drummer being referred to here.

 

• Naushad (Option 4): A pioneering Bollywood music director of the 1940s-60s era; he passed away in 2006, long before 2019.

question: The 'Joenpa Legso' is a welcome dance of _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhutan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Joenpa Legso is a traditional welcome dance of Bhutan, performed to greet dignitaries and honoured guests on important occasions. (जोएनपा लेग्सो — भूटान)

 

• The dance is performed by young Bhutanese women dressed in the traditional kira, symbolising hospitality and good wishes.

 

• It is commonly performed at official state functions, including during visits of foreign dignitaries to Bhutan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhutan's other well-known folk dances include the Black-Necked Crane Dance and mask dances (Cham dances) performed during festivals like Tshechu.

 

• Bhutan is known for its policy of measuring Gross National Happiness (GNH) instead of GDP as a development metric.

 

NOTE

 

• Afghanistan (Option 1): Known for folk dances such as Attan, not Joenpa Legso.

 

• Sri Lanka (Option 3): Known for dances such as Kandyan dance and Ves dance.

 

• Bangladesh (Option 4): Known for folk dances such as Baul dance, not Joenpa Legso.

question: Following an order of 16 July 2021, the Supreme Court of India introduced an electronic system named ____________, in November 2021, through which its crucial decisions can be communicated electronically to prison authorities and investigating agencies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is FASTER.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• FASTER stands for Fast and Secured Transmission of Electronic Records. (फास्टर प्रणाली — सुप्रीम कोर्ट)

 

• It was launched by the Supreme Court of India in November 2021, following its own order dated 16 July 2021, to ensure secure and instantaneous electronic transmission of court orders such as bail orders and stay orders to prison authorities and investigating agencies.

 

• The system was introduced to prevent undue delays in the release of undertrials/convicts after grant of bail, which often occurred because of the time taken for physical transmission of orders.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The FASTER system uses digitally signed electronic records transmitted via a secure, encrypted channel directly to designated nodal officers of prisons, police, and investigating agencies.

 

• It was launched in the backdrop of a case involving the death of a convict who remained in jail despite a stay on his execution, which was communicated late.

 

NOTE

 

• INSTANT, RAPID, QUICKER (Options 1, 3, 4): These are not the actual name of the Supreme Court's electronic transmission system; the correct official name is FASTER.

question: Select the correct statement from the given options.
option_1: There is very little temperature difference between day and night in the coastal areas of Kerala.
option_2: There is very little temperature difference between day and night in Rajasthan.
option_3: There is extreme cold in southern India during winter season.
option_4: There is plenty of rain observed in central India throughout the year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is There is very little temperature difference between day and night in the coastal areas of Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Coastal areas of Kerala experience a maritime/equable climate due to the moderating influence of the sea, which keeps the diurnal (day-night) temperature range small. (केरल तटीय क्षेत्र — सम जलवायु)

 

• Water heats up and cools down much more slowly than land, so coastal regions do not show the sharp day-night temperature swings seen in continental/desert areas.

 

• Kerala, being a narrow coastal strip bordered by the Arabian Sea, therefore has a relatively uniform temperature throughout the day and night.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Areas with a continental climate, such as deserts, show the opposite effect — very high diurnal temperature range because land heats and cools quickly.

 

• India's climate is broadly classified as a tropical monsoon type, but regional variations exist due to relief, distance from the sea, and altitude.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan (Option 2): Being an arid, continental region far from the sea's moderating effect, Rajasthan actually shows a very large difference between day and night temperatures, not a small one.

 

• Southern India (Option 3): Peninsular/southern India, being surrounded by the sea on three sides, does not experience extreme cold in winter; winters there are generally mild.

 

• Central India (Option 4): Central India receives rainfall mainly during the south-west monsoon (June-September), not throughout the year.

question: By what name did Allauddin Khilji build his capital?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Siri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alauddin Khalji, the second ruler of the Khalji dynasty, founded the city of Siri as his new capital near Delhi. (सीरी — अलाउद्दीन खिलजी)

 

• Siri was built to defend against repeated Mongol invasions and is considered the second of the seven historic cities of Delhi.

 

• Alauddin Khalji also established a garrison town, Siri Fort, whose ruins survive near present-day Delhi (Shahpur Jat/Siri Fort area).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alauddin Khalji is also known for his market control policies and successful campaigns against the Mongols, as well as his conquests in the Deccan.

 

• The seven cities of Delhi in chronological order (traditionally) include Lal Kot/Qila Rai Pithora, Siri, Tughlaqabad, Jahanpanah, Firozabad, Purana Qila (Dinpanah), and Shahjahanabad.

 

NOTE

 

• Khijrabad (Option 1): Not a capital built by Alauddin Khalji; associated instead with later Delhi Sultanate/Sayyid-era references.

 

• Dinpanah (Option 3): Built by the Mughal emperor Humayun, later developed as Purana Qila.

 

• Rajpithora (Option 4): Refers to Qila Rai Pithora, built by Prithviraj Chauhan, the first of the seven cities of Delhi.

question: Narali Poornima marks the end of monsoon season in which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Narali Poornima (Coconut Full Moon festival) is celebrated mainly by the fishing communities of the coastal regions of Maharashtra, marking the symbolic end of the monsoon season. (नारळी पौर्णिमा — महाराष्ट्र)

 

• On this day, fisherfolk offer coconuts (nariyal) to the Sea God (Varuna) to seek his blessings before resuming sea voyages and fishing activities after the monsoon.

 

• It falls on the full moon day (Poornima) of the Hindu month of Shravan, and coincides with Raksha Bandhan in many regions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Narali Poornima is especially significant in coastal districts of Maharashtra such as Mumbai, Konkan, and Ratnagiri.

 

• Other Maharashtrian festivals tied to the agricultural/monsoon calendar include Bail Pola and Gudi Padwa.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 1): Not associated with Narali Poornima; known instead for festivals like Chhath Puja.

 

• West Bengal (Option 2): Celebrates its own set of festivals such as Rakhi Purnima/Jhulan Purnima, distinct from Narali Poornima.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Not associated with Narali Poornima, which is specific to Maharashtra's coastal fishing communities.

question: Dhalo is a folk dance of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dhalo (also spelt Dhalo'o) is a traditional folk dance of Goa, performed by women during the winter months, especially around the Paush month (December-January). (ढालो नृत्य — गोवा)

 

• It is performed in the courtyards of homes at night, with women dancing in a circle and singing devotional/folk songs, often dedicated to local deities.

 

• The dance is closely associated with Goan Hindu village traditions and community bonding.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important folk dances of Goa include Fugdi, Ghode Modni, Corridinho, and Dekhni.

 

• Goa's culture reflects a blend of Indo-Portuguese influences owing to nearly 450 years of Portuguese colonial rule.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 1): Known for folk dances such as Karagattam and Kolattam, not Dhalo.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 2): Known for dances such as Raslila and Kajri, not Dhalo.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Known for tribal dances such as Karma and Saila, not Dhalo.

question: The policy of dual system of government of Bengal was the brainchild of which Governor-General?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Clive.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dual Government System in Bengal was introduced by Robert Clive (Lord Clive) in 1765, after the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha to the East India Company via the Treaty of Allahabad. (द्वैध शासन प्रणाली — लॉर्ड क्लाइव)

 

• Under this system, the Company held the Diwani (revenue collection) rights while the Nizamat (administrative/judicial) responsibility remained with the Nawab, though real power lay with the Company without direct accountability.

 

• This system led to widespread exploitation and misgovernance, contributing to the devastating Bengal Famine of 1770.

 

• The Dual Government was eventually abolished in 1772 by Warren Hastings, who took over direct administration on behalf of the Company.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Robert Clive is also known for his victory in the Battle of Plassey (1757) and the Battle of Buxar (1764) aftermath negotiations that secured the Diwani.

 

• Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1772 and abolished the dual system of government.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Hastings (Option 1): Known for the Third Anglo-Maratha War and paramountcy policy, not the dual government system.

 

• Lord Lytton (Option 3): Known for the Vernacular Press Act (1878) and Second Anglo-Afghan War.

 

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 4): Known for the Doctrine of Lapse and expansion of railways/telegraph in India.

question: Identify the ODD one out.
solution_text:
The correct answer is White revolution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Modern agricultural technology, Green revolution, and seed-fertiliser-water technology are all directly linked to the increase in foodgrain/crop production in India. (श्वेत क्रांति — दूध उत्पादन)

 

• The Green Revolution, led by M.S. Swaminathan and based on high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilisers, and irrigation (the seed-fertiliser-water package), was itself a form of modern agricultural technology aimed at boosting crop yields, especially wheat and rice.

 

• The White Revolution, on the other hand, refers to Operation Flood, led by Verghese Kurien, which was aimed at increasing milk production/dairy development, not crop agriculture — making it the odd one out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India became the world's largest milk producer as a result of the White Revolution/Operation Flood, launched in 1970.

 

• The Green Revolution in India began in the mid-1960s, primarily in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Modern agricultural technology, Green revolution, Seed-fertiliser-water technology (Options 1, 3, 4): All three relate to techniques and strategies used to boost crop/foodgrain production, unlike the White Revolution which pertains to milk/dairy production.

question: In which of the following years did the Indian Premier League begin?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2008.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Premier League (IPL), a Twenty20 cricket league, was founded by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and began its inaugural season in 2008. (आईपीएल — 2008 में शुरू)

 

• The first IPL match was played on 18 April 2008, between Kolkata Knight Riders and Royal Challengers Bangalore.

 

• The first IPL season (2008) was won by the Rajasthan Royals, captained by Shane Warne.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The concept of IPL was conceived by Lalit Modi, who served as its founding chairman and commissioner.

 

• Owing to the 2009 Indian general elections, the second season of IPL (2009) was held in South Africa instead of India.

 

NOTE

 

• 2010, 2007, 2009 (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these mark the actual founding year of the IPL; the league was founded and began play in 2008.

question: The FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022 was hosted by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022 was hosted by India, marking the first time India hosted a FIFA World Cup event (a men's edition, the U-17 Men's World Cup, had earlier been hosted by India in 2017). (फीफा अंडर-17 महिला विश्व कप 2022 — भारत)

 

• The tournament was held across venues in Bhubaneswar, Goa, and Navi Mumbai in October-November 2022.

 

• The champion of the 2022 edition was Spain, who defeated Colombia in the final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India had earlier hosted the FIFA U-17 Men's World Cup in 2017, won by England.

 

• The Golden Boot at the 2022 U-17 Women's World Cup was won by Linda Caicedo of Colombia.

 

NOTE

 

• Qatar (Option 1): Hosted the FIFA Men's World Cup 2022, not the U-17 Women's edition.

 

• Bangladesh (Option 2): Not the host of the 2022 tournament.

 

• Indonesia (Option 4): Was originally slated to host the FIFA U-20 World Cup 2023 (later withdrawn as host), not the 2022 U-17 Women's World Cup.

question: In which state is the Gorumara National Park located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gorumara National Park is located in the Dooars region of West Bengal, in the Jalpaiguri district, along the banks of the Murti and Raidak rivers. (गोरुमारा राष्ट्रीय उद्यान — पश्चिम बंगाल)

 

• It is renowned for its healthy population of the Indian one-horned rhinoceros and is often called a model of successful conservation in India.

 

• The park was declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1949 and later upgraded to National Park status in 1994.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important national parks of West Bengal include Jaldapara National Park, Buxa Tiger Reserve, and Sundarbans National Park.

 

• The Sundarbans National Park in West Bengal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and famous for the Royal Bengal Tiger.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 1): Home to national parks like Kaziranga and Manas, not Gorumara.

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 3): Home to Jim Corbett National Park and Rajaji National Park, not Gorumara.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Home to Valmiki National Park, not Gorumara.

question: Mrinalini Vikram Sarabhai, the Bharatanatyam legend, was also recognised for which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mrinalini Sarabhai was a legendary Indian classical dancer trained in both Bharatanatyam (under Meenakshisundaram Pillai and others) and Kathakali (under Guru Thakazhi Kunchu Kurup). (मृणालिनी साराभाई — भरतनाट्यम व कथकली)

 

• She founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad in 1949, which remains a leading institution for dance and theatre training in India.

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1992) for her contributions to Indian classical dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mrinalini Sarabhai was married to the eminent scientist Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, known as the father of the Indian space programme.

 

• Their daughter, Mallika Sarabhai, is also a celebrated classical dancer and social activist.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 1): A classical dance form of North India, associated with exponents like Birju Maharaj, not Mrinalini Sarabhai's primary training.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 3): A classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, associated with exponents like Yamini Krishnamurthy, not Mrinalini Sarabhai.

 

• Odissi (Option 4): A classical dance form of Odisha, associated with exponents like Kelucharan Mohapatra, not Mrinalini Sarabhai.

question: In which period is the first inscriptional example of the practice of Sati found?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gupta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The earliest known inscriptional evidence of the practice of Sati is the Eran inscription (510 CE) from the reign of the Gupta ruler Bhanugupta, found in present-day Madhya Pradesh. (सती प्रथा का प्रथम अभिलेखीय साक्ष्य — गुप्त काल)

 

• The inscription commemorates the death of Goparaja, a general of Bhanugupta, whose wife is recorded to have immolated herself on his funeral pyre.

 

• Although literary references to self-immolation exist from earlier periods, the Eran inscription is considered the first epigraphic (inscriptional) record of the practice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gupta period (c. 320-550 CE) is often called the 'Golden Age' of ancient India due to advances in art, science, literature, and administration.

 

• The practice of Sati was later formally abolished in 1829 through the efforts of Raja Ram Mohan Roy and Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.

 

NOTE

 

• Maukhari, Vardhana, Satavahana (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these dynasties are associated with the earliest inscriptional record of Sati; that distinction belongs to the Gupta period's Eran inscription.

question: Choose the correct set of the names for the organic compounds in the given figure.
option_1: a: Furan, b: Toluene, c: Pyridine
option_2: a: Furan, b: Pyridine, c: Thiophene
option_3: a: Furan, b: Thiophene, c: Aniline
option_4: a: Anisole, b: Thiophene, c: Pyridine
solution_text:
The correct answer is a: Furan, b: Pyridine, c: Thiophene.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The figure shows three five/six-membered heterocyclic organic compounds, each identifiable by the heteroatom present in its ring. (फ्यूरान, पिरिडीन, थायोफीन — विषमचक्रीय यौगिक)

 

• Compound (a) is a five-membered ring containing an oxygen (O) atom — this is Furan.

 

• Compound (b) is a six-membered ring containing a nitrogen (N) atom — this is Pyridine.

 

• Compound (c) is a five-membered ring containing a sulphur (S) atom — this is Thiophene.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Furan, Pyridine, and Thiophene are all classic examples of aromatic heterocyclic compounds studied in organic chemistry.

 

• Pyridine is structurally similar to benzene but with one CH group replaced by nitrogen, and it is commonly used as a solvent and base in organic synthesis.

 

NOTE

 

• Toluene (Option 1, part b): This is methylbenzene, a simple aromatic hydrocarbon with no heteroatom in the ring — it does not match the nitrogen-containing ring shown in (b).

 

• Aniline (Option 3, part c): This is aminobenzene (a benzene ring with an -NH2 group), not the sulphur-containing five-membered ring shown in (c).

 

• Anisole (Option 4, part a): This is methoxybenzene, a benzene derivative, not the oxygen-containing five-membered ring shown in (a).

question: In 1942, the British government sent the ________ mission to India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cripps.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In March 1942, the British government sent the Cripps Mission, led by Sir Stafford Cripps, to India to negotiate Indian cooperation in the Second World War in exchange for a promise of Dominion Status after the war. (क्रिप्स मिशन — 1942)

 

• The mission's proposals were rejected by the Indian National Congress, which famously described it as 'a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank' (a remark attributed to Mahatma Gandhi).

 

• Its failure directly led to the launch of the Quit India Movement in August 1942.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Cabinet Mission came later, in 1946, led by three British cabinet ministers, and proposed a federal structure for a united India.

 

• Lord Linlithgow was the Viceroy of India during 1936-1943, under whose tenure the Cripps Mission and Quit India Movement occurred.

 

NOTE

 

• Linlithgow (Option 2): Name of the Viceroy of India at the time, not the name of a 1942 mission.

 

• Cabinet (Option 3): The Cabinet Mission was sent in 1946, not 1942.

 

• Lansdowne (Option 4): Refers to Lord Lansdowne, a Viceroy of India in the late 19th century, unrelated to any 1942 mission.

question: Which state ranked first among the 18 large and mid-sized states (with population of over one crore each) in justice delivery in India as per the second edition of the India Justice Report?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The India Justice Report (IJR) 2020, its second edition, ranked Maharashtra first among the 18 large and mid-sized states in overall justice delivery. (इंडिया जस्टिस रिपोर्ट, दूसरा संस्करण — महाराष्ट्र प्रथम)

 

• The report, published by Tata Trusts in collaboration with several partner organisations, ranks states on the performance of the police, judiciary, prisons, and legal aid pillars.

 

• Tamil Nadu was ranked second in the second edition (2020) of the report.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first edition (IJR 2019) was also topped by Maharashtra, showing consistency in its justice-delivery performance.

 

• The third edition (IJR 2022) saw Karnataka rank first among large and mid-sized states, a change from the earlier two editions.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 2): Ranked second in the second edition, not first.

 

• West Bengal (Option 3): Did not rank first in the second edition of the report.

 

• Karnataka (Option 4): Topped the third edition (2022) of the India Justice Report, not the second edition being asked about here.

question: What is the duty of the Chief Minister, as mentioned under Article 167 of the Indian Constitution?
option_1: Communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
option_2: Appointment and removal of Council of the Ministers.
option_3: Appointment of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
option_4: Appointment of Advocate General of the state in consultation with Attorney general.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 167 of the Indian Constitution lays down the duties of the Chief Minister with respect to furnishing information to the Governor of the state. (अनुच्छेद 167 — मुख्यमंत्री का कर्तव्य)

 

• It duty-binds the Chief Minister to communicate to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of the affairs of the state and proposals for legislation.

 

• It also requires the CM to furnish such information relating to the administration of the state as the Governor may call for, and to submit for consideration matters on which a decision has been taken by a minister individually but not considered by the Council.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Governor of a state is appointed under Article 153, and the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister is dealt with under Article 163 and 164.

 

• Article 167 is analogous to Article 78, which lays down similar duties of the Prime Minister towards the President at the Union level.

 

NOTE

 

• Appointment/removal of Council of Ministers (Option 2): This power lies with the Governor, acting on the advice of the Chief Minister, and is dealt with under Article 164, not Article 167.

 

• Appointment of the Speaker (Option 3): The Speaker is elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly, not appointed by the CM under Article 167.

 

• Appointment of Advocate General (Option 4): This is dealt with under Article 165, which empowers the Governor to appoint the Advocate General, not Article 167.

question: Which water-soluble pigment belonging to a phenolic group is present in pomegranate, eggplant, black carrots and red cabbage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anthocyanins.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Anthocyanins are water-soluble pigments belonging to the flavonoid (phenolic) group, responsible for the red, purple, and blue colours seen in many fruits and vegetables. (एंथोसायनिन — जल-घुलनशील वर्णक)

 

• They are found in pomegranate, eggplant (brinjal), black carrots, red cabbage, blueberries, and grapes, among other produce.

 

• Anthocyanins are also valued as antioxidants and change colour with pH — appearing red in acidic conditions and blue/purple in alkaline conditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Betalains are also water-soluble pigments but are found in plants like beetroot and amaranth, and are chemically distinct from anthocyanins (nitrogen-containing).

 

• Anthocyanins are used commercially as natural food colourants and are studied for potential health benefits including anti-inflammatory properties.

 

NOTE

 

• Phycoerythrin (Option 1): A red pigment-protein complex found in red algae and cyanobacteria, not in the fruits/vegetables mentioned.

 

• Phycobilins (Option 2): Light-harvesting pigments found in cyanobacteria, red algae, and glaucophytes, unrelated to the fruits/vegetables mentioned.

 

• Betalains (Option 3): Present in plants such as beetroot, but not the specific group (pomegranate, eggplant, black carrots, red cabbage) described in the question, which are anthocyanin-rich.

question:
Match the columns.

Column-A (Disorder): i. Gaucher disease  ii. Hunter syndrome  iii. Tay-Sachs disease  iv. Phenylketonuria

Column-B (Enzyme): a. Phenylalanine hydroxylase  b. Hexosaminidase A  c. Iduronate-2-sulfatase  d. Glucocerebrosidase
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• These are all genetic metabolic disorders caused by deficiency of a specific enzyme, and each disorder is matched to its correct deficient enzyme. (आनुवंशिक चयापचय विकार — एंजाइम की कमी)

 

• Gaucher disease (i) is caused by deficiency of the enzyme Glucocerebrosidase (d), leading to accumulation of glucocerebroside in cells.

 

• Hunter syndrome (ii) is caused by deficiency of Iduronate-2-sulfatase (c), a mucopolysaccharidosis (MPS II).

 

• Tay-Sachs disease (iii) is caused by deficiency of Hexosaminidase A (b), leading to accumulation of GM2 ganglioside in neurons.

 

• Phenylketonuria (iv) is caused by deficiency of Phenylalanine hydroxylase (a), leading to accumulation of phenylalanine in the body.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Phenylketonuria (PKU) is routinely screened for in newborns and managed through a low-phenylalanine diet.

 

• Gaucher disease is the most common lysosomal storage disorder and can be treated with enzyme replacement therapy.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2, and 4: Each of these combinations mismatches at least one disorder with the wrong enzyme; only the mapping i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a is correct for all four disorder-enzyme pairs.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution prohibits religious instructions in any state-funded educational institution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 28.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 28 of the Indian Constitution provides for 'Freedom as to attendance at religious instruction or religious worship in certain educational institutions.' (अनुच्छेद 28 — धार्मिक शिक्षा पर प्रतिबंध)

 

• Clause (1) of Article 28 states that no religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.

 

• However, this restriction does not apply to institutions administered by the State but established under an endowment or trust that requires religious instruction (Clause 2), and other institutions must have voluntary consent for attending religious instruction (Clause 3).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Articles 25 to 28 collectively guarantee the Right to Freedom of Religion as one of the Fundamental Rights under the Indian Constitution.

 

• Article 30 separately protects the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 29 (Option 2): Protects the cultural and educational rights of minorities, specifically the right to conserve language, script, or culture.

 

• Article 30 (Option 3): Grants minorities the right to establish and administer their own educational institutions.

 

• Article 27 (Option 4): States that no person shall be compelled to pay any taxes for promotion of a particular religion.

question: Which of the followings is NOT an example of factor payment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pension.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A factor payment is a reward given for rendering productive services by a factor of production during the current period, in the process of production of goods and services. (कारक भुगतान — उत्पादन के साधनों को पुरस्कार)

 

• Wages (payment for labour), Interest (payment for capital), and Rent (payment for land) are all classic examples of factor payments, as they are made in exchange for a current productive contribution.

 

• Pension, on the other hand, is a transfer payment — it is paid without any corresponding current productive service being rendered by the recipient (it relates to past service).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of transfer payments include scholarships, unemployment allowance, and old-age pensions.

 

• National Income (NI) is calculated by summing up all factor payments made within a country/by its residents during an accounting year — transfer payments are excluded from this calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• Interest, Wages, Rent (Options 1, 2, 3): All three are genuine factor payments, made in return for capital, labour, and land respectively used in current production.

question: Which is the largest container port in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru Port.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT), located at Nhava Sheva near Mumbai, Maharashtra, is India's largest container port, handling a majority of the country's containerised cargo traffic. (जवाहरलाल नेहरू पत्तन — सबसे बड़ा कंटेनर पोर्ट)

 

• It is a major port under the direct control of the Government of India and is one of the busiest ports in South Asia.

 

• JNPT was commissioned in 1989 to decongest the older Mumbai Port.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India currently has 12 major ports, including Kandla (Deendayal), Mumbai, JNPT, Mormugao, New Mangalore, Cochin, Chennai, Kamarajar (Ennore), V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin), Visakhapatnam, Paradip, and Kolkata (Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port).

 

• JNPT has since been renamed the Nhava Sheva - Jawaharlal Nehru Port (NSJNP).

 

NOTE

 

• Kandla Port (Option 1): A major port in Gujarat, primarily known for bulk cargo, not the largest container handler.

 

• Kolkata Port (Option 3): India's oldest operating major port, located on the Hooghly river, but not the largest container port.

 

• Hazira Port (Option 4): A private port in Gujarat, not the largest container port in India.

question: Which sportsperson was named by homegrown pharma major Lupin Ltd as a brand ambassador for its Shakti campaign in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mary Kom.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 2022, pharmaceutical company Lupin Ltd named boxing legend Mary Kom as the brand ambassador for its 'Shakti' campaign. (मैरी कॉम — लुपिन शक्ति अभियान)

 

• The Shakti campaign was launched to raise awareness about cardiovascular disease among women in India.

 

• Mary Kom, a six-time World Boxing Champion and Olympic bronze medallist, was chosen for her image as a symbol of strength and resilience, aligning with the campaign's message.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mary Kom hails from Manipur and has also been honoured with the Padma Vibhushan, Rajya Sabha nomination, and the Khel Ratna award.

 

• Lupin Ltd is one of India's leading pharmaceutical companies, known for its work in cardiovascular and other therapeutic areas.

 

NOTE

 

• Rahul Dravid (Option 1): A former Indian cricketer and coach, not associated with the Lupin Shakti campaign.

 

• Mithali Raj (Option 2): A former Indian women's cricket team captain, not the face of this particular campaign.

 

• PV Sindhu (Option 4): A celebrated Indian badminton player, not named as the Shakti campaign's brand ambassador in 2022.

question: Which physical unit is defined as the intensity of a field that produces a force of one newton (N) per ampere (A) per metre for a conductor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tesla.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tesla (T) is the SI unit of magnetic flux density (magnetic field strength), defined such that a field of one Tesla exerts a force of one newton (N) on a conductor carrying one ampere (A) of current per metre of its length, when the conductor is placed perpendicular to the field. (टेस्ला — चुंबकीय क्षेत्र की तीव्रता की इकाई)

 

• Mathematically, 1 Tesla = 1 N / (A·m) = 1 Wb/m² = 1 kg/(A·s²).

 

• It is named after the physicist and engineer Nikola Tesla, in recognition of his contributions to the study of electromagnetism.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tesla is derived from the Weber (Wb), the SI unit of magnetic flux, where 1 Tesla equals 1 Weber per square metre.

 

• Devices such as MRI machines typically operate with magnetic field strengths measured in Tesla (commonly 1.5 T to 3 T).

 

NOTE

 

• Candela (Option 1): The SI unit of luminous intensity, unrelated to magnetic fields.

 

• Coulomb (Option 2): The SI unit of electric charge, not magnetic field intensity.

 

• Pascal (Option 4): The SI unit of pressure/stress, not magnetic field intensity.
